translationRepairs: On renshen, Shu forces raided the western frontier; the bandits Zhang Da, Ren Kang, and others seized Qingshui Defe Iron Castle to join them.
On renshen, Shu forces raided the western frontier; the bandits Zhang Da, Ren Kang, and others seized the fortress of Qingshui Defe to join them.
Chinese 清水德鐵之城 is a place-name fortress, not 'Qingshui Defe Iron Castle' as if Iron were a separate English gloss.
On renshen, Shu people raided the western border; bandits Zhang Da, Ren Kang, and others plundered Qingshui Defe Iron Castle in response.
On renshen, Shu people raided the western border; bandits Zhang Da, Ren Kang, and others seized the city of Qingshui Defe in response.
Same place-name issue as idiomatic: 德鐵 should not be split into Defe Iron.

On gengyin, Yang Yanshou—former Right Mentor to the Heir Apparent among the two fallen dynasties and hereditary Duke of Xi—was appointed Left Mentor to the Crown Prince; Yuwen Hao, magistrate of Xiangcheng in Ruzhou among the three lineages of former rulers and hereditary Duke of Jie, was granted an additional three thousand households in his fief.

On gengyin, Yang Yanshou—former Right Mentor to the Heir Apparent among the two fallen dynasties and hereditary Duke of Xi—was appointed Left Mentor to the Crown Prince; Yuwen Jie, magistrate of Xiangcheng in Ruzhou among the three lineages of former rulers and hereditary Duke of Jie, was granted an additional three thousand households in his fief.
Chinese 宇文頡 is Yuwen Jie (Jié); Hao misreads 頡.

On gengyin, Yang Yanshou, former Right Mentor to the Heir Apparent of the two deposed dynasties and hereditary Duke of Xi, was made Left Mentor to the Crown Prince; Yuwen Hao, magistrate of Xiangcheng in Ruzhou of the three lineages of former rulers and hereditary Duke of Jie, received an additional fief of three thousand households.

On gengyin, Yang Yanshou, former Right Mentor to the Heir Apparent of the two deposed dynasties and hereditary Duke of Xi, was made Left Mentor to the Crown Prince; Yuwen Jie, magistrate of Xiangcheng in Ruzhou of the three lineages of former rulers and hereditary Duke of Jie, received an additional fief of three thousand households.
Chinese 宇文頡 is Yuwen Jie; both English fields wrongly say Hao.

On bingshen, Hedong military governor An Shenxin reported: "Officers Kang Congshou, Li Chong, Sun Dayu, Zhang Chong, Yu Qian, and others rose in mutiny with the men under their command; the disturbance was quickly put down, with five hundred dead."

On bingshen, Hezhong military governor An Shenxin reported: "Officers Kang Congshou, Li Chong, Sun Dayu, Zhang Chong, Yu Qian, and others rose in mutiny with the men under their command; the disturbance was quickly put down, with five hundred dead."
Chinese 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong (河東).

On bingshen, Hedong military governor An Shenxin reported: "The military officers Kang Congshou, Li Chong, Sun Dayu, Zhang Chong, Yu Qian, and others incited mutiny with the troops under their command; it was soon suppressed, with five hundred dead."

Du Chongwei, military governor of Xu Prefecture, became military governor of Yun Prefecture, and An Shenxin, military governor of Hezhong, became military governor of Xu Prefecture.
鄆州 is Yun, not Yan; 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong.

On guiyou, Wang Jianli, military governor of Qingzhou, was appointed military governor of the Zhaoyi Army and advanced to Prince of Han. Liao and Qin prefectures were detached as dependencies of Zhaoyi so that Jianli, a native of Liao, might enjoy the glory of returning home in splendor.

On guiyou, Wang Jianli, military governor of Qingzhou, was appointed military governor of the Zhaoyi Army and advanced to Prince of Han. Liao and Qin prefectures were detached as dependencies of Zhaoyi so that Jianli, a native of Liaozhou, might enjoy the glory of returning home in splendor.
沁州 is Qin/Qinzhou (Qìn); keep place sense clear as Liaozhou native.
The emperor said, "What crime have these men committed? Give them generous provisions and send them home."
The emperor said: "What crime have these men committed? Give them generous provisions and send them home."
Chinese uses colon-like 曰 and quote; English comma splice mildly obscures speech boundary—prefer colon and quotes matching Chinese.

On bingshen, an edict declared: the late Qian Hongxun, Military Commissioner of Jinghai Army and concurrently Pacification and Disposition Commissioner of the Southeast, Acting Grand Master and Prefect of Wen, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; the late Qian Hongfu, Deputy Military Commissioner of the Two Armies of Wuyue and Acting Grand Commandant, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

Chinese 錢宏僔 is Hongzun (僔); Hongfu mismatches the character.

On wuyin, Tang Shuyu was enfeoffed as Prince of Xing'an, the spirit Taidai as Duke of Changning, and Supervising Censor Zhang Cuan and Department Director Zhang Shousu were dispatched to perform the investiture rites on the spot.

On wuyin, Tang Shuyu was enfeoffed as Prince of Xing'an, the spirit Taidai as Duke of Changning, and Supervising Censor Zhang Tuan and Department Director Zhang Shousu were dispatched to perform the investiture rites on the spot.
Chinese 張彖 is Zhang Tuan; Cuan misreads 彖.
On renyin, Zhang Cuan, Commissioner for the Sanbai Canal System, became Supervising Censor.
On renyin, Zhang Tuan, Commissioner for the Sanbai Canal System, became Supervising Censor.
